claims.title: Finite-mass Landau-Coulomb: continuation criteria, Fisher growth and heat covariance

quoted_fields.interface: Velocity R3, m_i>0 FINITE, c_ij=c_ji>0, strictly positive Schwartz data with actual n_i=int f_i>0 and finite I_m=sum m_i^-1 int |grad f_i|^2/f_i. a(z)=P_z/|z|, b=div a=-2z/|z|^3. Physical equation partial_t f_i=sum_j[c_ij/m_i^2 div(A[f_j] grad f_i)-c_ij/(m_i m_j)div(f_i(b*f_j))]. Conditional criteria apply on the actual local strong weighted-L2 solution class. Auxiliary P_tau^i=exp((tau/m_i)Delta) uses HEAT time tau, separate from physical collision time. Particle numbers and mass-weighted detailed balance remain explicit.
quoted_fields.failure: Global finite-mass Coulomb well-posedness is UNRESOLVED. Increasing Fisher information disproves universal monotonicity only, not regularity; the construction keeps finite recoil. Zhu2512.17905v1 cross |gamma|<=sqrt(8) excludes Coulomb -3; Junne-Winter-Yoldas2512.17082v1 local theory and compensated infinite-ion theorem are distinct, with its extra condition retained. The newer entropy-dissipation example supplies no dissipation monotonicity. N757 has a cutoff/supplied regularity; N1763 concerns quantum Landau-Fermi-Dirac in an already-global class. No pending unidentified fulltext is a premise/recovery route. E_s has no proved collision growth/sign bound, and full heat-range differentiation is formal until endpoint estimates close. Generic two-point covariance negativity is not a physical product-score counterexample.
